content.title: Trump’s 50-Year Mortgage Loses Steam as Industry Questions Costs
content.summary: “All it means is you pay less per month,” Trump said in an interview that aired on Monday.  Paying for a home over five decades would increase the amount of interest homeowners would pay while slowing the amount of equity they build in their homes.  “A 50-year mortgage dramatically depreciates the biggest value of homeownership — wealth building,” said David Dworkin, president and CEO of the National Housing Conference.

content.title: White House's 50-year mortgage proposal has one notable benefit but a number of drawbacks
content.summary: The White House says it is considering backing a 50-year mortgage to help alleviate the home affordability crisis in the country.  Bill Pulte, director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, said on X over the weekend that a 50-year mortgage would be “a complete game changer” for homebuyers.  FHFA is the part of the federal government that oversees Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which buy and insure the vast majority of mortgages in the country.

content.title: Heard on the Street Monday Recap: Risk On Again
content.summary: Stocks rallied after the Senate advanced a measure designed to end the government shutdown.  Magnificent Seven companies and other technology stocks led the way.  The Nasdaq composite gained 2.3%, while the S&P 500 rose 1.5% and the Dow industrials climbed 0.8%.
